tools.name: agents
tools.description: Manage agent registries, definitions, and execution runs. Agents are single-task executors that claim a task, work it, and complete it. Use registry actions to manage agent sources (Foundry, FileSystem, Catalog). Use definition actions to list/create/update/delete agents. Use tools.list to discover available tools (SDK, catalog, host) before creating or updating an agent — it returns tool names grouped by category with pre-built grant hints you can pass to assign-tools or include in create/update. Use run actions to execute agents against tasks.

agentId.description: Agent ID (registry/name) for get, update, delete, run.start.

toolReferences.description: Tool reference names the agent can use.

toolGrants.description: Declarative tool grants for create, update, or assign-tools. Use tools.list to discover available tools and their grant hints.

query.description: Search filter for tools.list (matches name, description, or source).

runId.description: Run ID for run.get, run.outputs, run.cancel.

tools.name: agentSessions
tools.description: Inspect and manage ACP-native agent sessions. Use 'list' to get session summaries filtered by status/agentId/taskId. Use 'get' for full session detail including permission state. Use 'timeline' or 'tail' for incremental output retrieval with cursor-based polling. Use 'cancel' to stop an active session. Use 'permissionState' to read the pending permission prompt when status is permissionNeeded.

sessionId.description: Session ID for get, timeline, tail, cancel, permissionState.

limit.description: Maximum sessions to return (list) or timeline entries per page (timeline/tail).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous timeline/tail response for incremental polling.

tools.name: bookshelf
tools.description: Interact with Discovery document bookshelves across the full lifecycle: knowledge base CRUD, ingest/indexing controls, content add/remove, search/ask, health/status, directory watch, loader planning/runs, resolver configuration, and embeddings.

action.description: The bookshelf operation to perform. Supports full knowledge base lifecycle operations including CRUD, ingest/indexing controls, search/ask, health/status, directory watch, loader planning/runs, resolver config, and embeddings.

name.description: Knowledge base name (required for create action, e.g. 'Engine Logs')

description.description: Knowledge base description (optional, for create action)

directory.description: Absolute path to a folder to watch for changes

directoryWatch.description: Optional: register a directory watch during knowledge base creation. Files in the directory will be automatically ingested and indexed.

query.description: Search/ask query text (required for ask and search actions)

shelves.description: Knowledge base names to scope the operation. If omitted, searches all enabled knowledge bases.

shelfId.description: Knowledge base ID or knowledge base name (case-insensitive) for get, remove, and ingest actions

strategy.description: Search strategy override (for ask and search)

includeSources.description: Include full source document content in responses (default: true for ask)

sourceRef.description: File or folder path to ingest

contentType.description: Optional content type hint (e.g. 'text/plain'). Not required — the system detects type automatically.

sources.description: Content sources to ingest. Each source needs a sourceRef (file/folder path).

tools.name: copilot_applyPatch
tools.description:
Edit text files. Do not use this tool to edit Jupyter notebooks. `apply_patch` allows you to execute a diff/patch against a text file, but the format of the diff specification is unique to this task, so pay careful attention to these instructions. To use the `apply_patch` command, you should pass a message of the following structure as "input":

*** Begin Patch
[YOUR_PATCH]
*** End Patch

Where [YOUR_PATCH] is the actual content of your patch, specified in the following V4A diff format.

*** [ACTION] File: [/absolute/path/to/file] -> ACTION can be one of Add, Update, or Delete.
An example of a message that you might pass as "input" to this function, in order to apply a patch, is shown below.

*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /Users/someone/pygorithm/searching/binary_search.py
@@class BaseClass
@@    def search():
-        pass
+        raise NotImplementedError()

@@class Subclass
@@    def search():
-        pass
+        raise NotImplementedError()

*** End Patch
Do not use line numbers in this diff format.

explanation.description: A short description of what the tool call is aiming to achieve.

tools.name: copilot_createDirectory
tools.description: Create a new directory structure in the workspace. Will recursively create all directories in the path, like mkdir -p. You do not need to use this tool before using create_file, that tool will automatically create the needed directories.

dirPath.description: The absolute path to the directory to create.

tools.name: copilot_createFile
tools.description: This is a tool for creating a new file in the workspace. The file will be created with the specified content. The directory will be created if it does not already exist. Never use this tool to edit a file that already exists.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file to create.

content.description: The content to write to the file.

tools.name: copilot_createNewJupyterNotebook
tools.description: Generates a new Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) in VS Code. Jupyter Notebooks are interactive documents commonly used for data exploration, analysis, visualization, and combining code with narrative text. Prefer creating plain Python files or similar unless a user explicitly requests creating a new Jupyter Notebook or already has a Jupyter Notebook opened or exists in the workspace.

query.description: The query to use to generate the jupyter notebook. This should be a clear and concise description of the notebook the user wants to create.

tools.name: copilot_createNewWorkspace
tools.description:
Get comprehensive setup steps to help the user create complete project structures in a VS Code workspace. This tool is designed for full project initialization and scaffolding, not for creating individual files.

When to use this tool:
- User wants to create a new complete project from scratch
- Setting up entire project frameworks (TypeScript projects, React apps, Node.js servers, etc.)
- Initializing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers with full structure
- Creating VS Code extensions with proper scaffolding
- Setting up Next.js, Vite, or other framework-based projects
- User asks for "new project", "create a workspace", "set up a [framework] project"
- Need to establish complete development environment with dependencies, config files, and folder structure

When NOT to use this tool:
- Creating single files or small code snippets
- Adding individual files to existing projects
- Making modifications to existing codebases
- User asks to "create a file" or "add a component"
- Simple code examples or demonstrations
- Debugging or fixing existing code

This tool provides complete project setup including:
- Folder structure creation
- Package.json and dependency management
- Configuration files (tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
- Initial boilerplate code
- Development environment setup
- Build and run instructions

Use other file creation tools for individual files within existing projects.

query.description: The query to use to generate the new workspace. This should be a clear and concise description of the workspace the user wants to create.

tools.name: copilot_editFiles
tools.description: This is a placeholder tool, do not use

tools.name: copilot_editNotebook
tools.description:
This is a tool for editing an existing Notebook file in the workspace. Generate the "explanation" property first.
The system is very smart and can understand how to apply your edits to the notebooks.
When updating the content of an existing cell, ensure newCode preserves whitespace and indentation exactly and does NOT include any code markers such as (...existing code...).

filePath.description: An absolute path to the notebook file to edit, or the URI of a untitled, not yet named, file, such as `untitled:Untitled-1.

cellId.description: Id of the cell that needs to be deleted or edited. Use the value `TOP`, `BOTTOM` when inserting a cell at the top or bottom of the notebook, else provide the id of the cell after which a new cell is to be inserted. Remember, if a cellId is provided and editType=insert, then a cell will be inserted after the cell with the provided cellId.

anyOf.description: The code for the new or existing cell to be edited. Code should not be wrapped within <VSCode.Cell> tags. Do NOT include code markers such as (...existing code...) to indicate existing code.

items.description: The code for the new or existing cell to be edited. Code should not be wrapped within <VSCode.Cell> tags

language.description: The language of the cell. `markdown`, `python`, `javascript`, `julia`, etc.

editType.description:
The operation peformed on the cell, whether `insert`, `delete` or `edit`.
Use the `editType` field to specify the operation: `insert` to add a new cell, `edit` to modify an existing cell's content, and `delete` to remove a cell.

tools.name: copilot_fetchWebPage
tools.description: Fetches the main content from a web page. This tool is useful for summarizing or analyzing the content of a webpage. You should use this tool when you think the user is looking for information from a specific webpage.

urls.description: An array of URLs to fetch content from.

query.description: The query to search for in the web page's content. This should be a clear and concise description of the content you want to find.

tools.name: copilot_findFiles
tools.description:
Search for files in the workspace by glob pattern. This only returns the paths of matching files. Use this tool when you know the exact filename pattern of the files you're searching for. Glob patterns match from the root of the workspace folder. Examples:
- **/*.{js,ts} to match all js/ts files in the workspace.
- src/** to match all files under the top-level src folder.
- **/foo/**/*.js to match all js files under any foo folder in the workspace.

In a multi-root workspace, you can scope the search to a specific workspace folder by using the absolute path to the folder as the query, e.g. /path/to/folder/**/*.ts.

query.description: Search for files with names or paths matching this glob pattern. Can also be an absolute path to a workspace folder to scope the search in a multi-root workspace.

maxResults.description: The maximum number of results to return. Do not use this unless necessary, it can slow things down. By default, only some matches are returned. If you use this and don't see what you're looking for, you can try again with a more specific query or a larger maxResults.

tools.name: copilot_findTestFiles
tools.description: For a source code file, find the file that contains the tests. For a test file find the file that contains the code under test.

tools.name: copilot_findTextInFiles
tools.description:
Do a fast text search in the workspace. Use this tool when you want to search with an exact string or regex. If you are not sure what words will appear in the workspace, prefer using regex patterns with alternation (|) or character classes to search for multiple potential words at once instead of making separate searches. For example, use 'function|method|procedure' to look for all of those words at once. Use includePattern to search within files matching a specific pattern, or in a specific file, using a relative path. Use 'includeIgnoredFiles' to include files normally ignored by .gitignore, other ignore files, and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower, only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs. Use this tool when you want to see an overview of a particular file, instead of using read_file many times to look for code within a file.

In a multi-root workspace, you can scope the search to a specific workspace folder by using the absolute path to the folder as the includePattern, e.g. /path/to/folder.

query.description: The pattern to search for in files in the workspace. Use regex with alternation (e.g., 'word1|word2|word3') or character classes to find multiple potential words in a single search. Be sure to set the isRegexp property properly to declare whether it's a regex or plain text pattern. Is case-insensitive.

isRegexp.description: Whether the pattern is a regex.

includePattern.description: Search files matching this glob pattern. Will be applied to the relative path of files within the workspace. To search recursively inside a folder, use a proper glob pattern like "src/folder/**". Do not use | in includePattern. Can also be an absolute path to a workspace folder to scope the search in a multi-root workspace.

maxResults.description: The maximum number of results to return. Do not use this unless necessary, it can slow things down. By default, only some matches are returned. If you use this and don't see what you're looking for, you can try again with a more specific query or a larger maxResults.

includeIgnoredFiles.description: Whether to include files that would normally be ignored according to .gitignore, other ignore files and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower. Only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs.

sourceControlState.description: The kinds of git state to filter by. Allowed values are: 'staged', 'unstaged', and 'merge-conflicts'. If not provided, all states will be included.

Use the tool to see the same errors that the user is seeing. If the user asks you to analyze all errors, or does not specify a file, use this tool to gather errors for all files. Also use this tool after editing a file to validate the change.

filePaths.description: The absolute paths to the files or folders to check for errors. Omit 'filePaths' when retrieving all errors.

tools.description: This is a tool returns the list of the Notebook cells along with the id, cell types, line ranges, language, execution information and output mime types for each cell. This is useful to get Cell Ids when executing a notebook or determine what cells have been executed and what order, or what cells have outputs. If required to read contents of a cell use this to determine the line range of a cells, and then use read_file tool to read a specific line range. Requery this tool if the contents of the notebook change.

filePath.description: An absolute path to the notebook file with the cell to run, or the URI of a untitled, not yet named, file, such as `untitled:Untitled-1.ipynb

tools.name: copilot_getProjectSetupInfo
tools.description: Do not call this tool without first calling the tool to create a workspace. This tool provides a project setup information for a Visual Studio Code workspace based on a project type and programming language.

projectType.description: The type of project to create. Supported values are: 'python-script', 'python-project', 'mcp-server', 'model-context-protocol-server', 'vscode-extension', 'next-js', 'vite' and 'other'

tools.name: copilot_getVSCodeAPI
tools.description:
Get comprehensive VS Code API documentation and references for extension development. This tool provides authoritative documentation for VS Code's extensive API surface, including proposed APIs, contribution points, and best practices. Use this tool for understanding complex VS Code API interactions.

When to use this tool:
- User asks about specific VS Code APIs, interfaces, or extension capabilities
- Need documentation for VS Code extension contribution points (commands, views, settings, etc.)
- Questions about proposed APIs and their usage patterns
- Understanding VS Code extension lifecycle, activation events, and packaging
- Best practices for VS Code extension development architecture
- API examples and code patterns for extension features
- Troubleshooting extension-specific issues or API limitations

When NOT to use this tool:
- Creating simple standalone files or scripts unrelated to VS Code extensions
- General programming questions not specific to VS Code extension development
- Questions about using VS Code as an editor (user-facing features)
- Non-extension related development tasks
- File creation or editing that doesn't involve VS Code extension APIs

CRITICAL usage guidelines:
1. Always include specific API names, interfaces, or concepts in your query
2. Mention the extension feature you're trying to implement
3. Include context about proposed vs stable APIs when relevant
4. Reference specific contribution points when asking about extension manifest
5. Be specific about the VS Code version or API version when known

Scope: This tool is for EXTENSION DEVELOPMENT ONLY - building tools that extend VS Code itself, not for general file creation or non-extension programming tasks.

query.description: The query to search vscode documentation for. Should contain all relevant context.

query.description: The keyword search query. Supports GitHub code search syntax such as 'language:typescript', 'extension:ts', 'path:src/', etc.

maxResults.description: Optional. The maximum number of search results to return. Defaults to 100.

tools.name: copilot_memory
tools.description:
Manage a persistent memory system with three scopes for storing notes and information across conversations.

Memory is organized under /memories/ with three tiers:
- `/memories/` — User memory: persistent notes that survive across all workspaces and conversations. Store preferences, patterns, and general insights here.
- `/memories/session/` — Session memory: notes scoped to the current conversation. Store task-specific context and in-progress notes here. Cleared after the conversation ends.
- `/memories/repo/` — Repository memory: repository-scoped facts stored via Copilot. Only the `create` command is supported for this path.

IMPORTANT: Before creating new memory files, first view the /memories/ directory to understand what already exists. This helps avoid duplicates and maintain organized notes.

Commands:
- `view`: View contents of a file or list directory contents. Can be used on files or directories (e.g., "/memories/" to see all top-level items).
- `create`: Create a new file at the specified path with the given content. Fails if the file already exists.
- `str_replace`: Replace an exact string in a file with a new string. The old_str must appear exactly once in the file.
- `insert`: Insert text at a specific line number in a file. Line 0 inserts at the beginning.
- `delete`: Delete a file or directory (and all its contents).
- `rename`: Rename or move a file or directory from path to new_path. Cannot rename across scopes.

command.description: The operation to perform on the memory file system.

path.description: The absolute path to the file or directory inside /memories/, e.g. "/memories/notes.md". Used by all commands except `rename`.

file_text.description: Required for `create`. The content of the file to create.

old_str.description: Required for `str_replace`. The exact string in the file to replace. Must appear exactly once.

new_str.description: Required for `str_replace`. The new string to replace old_str with.

insert_line.description: Required for `insert`. The 0-based line number to insert text at. 0 inserts before the first line.

insert_text.description: Required for `insert`. The text to insert at the specified line.

view_range.description: Optional for `view`. A two-element array [start_line, end_line] (1-indexed) to view a specific range of lines.

old_path.description: Required for `rename`. The current path of the file or directory to rename.

new_path.description: Required for `rename`. The new path for the file or directory.

tools.name: copilot_multiReplaceString
tools.description: This tool allows you to apply multiple replace_string_in_file operations in a single call, which is more efficient than calling replace_string_in_file multiple times. It takes an array of replacement operations and applies them sequentially. Each replacement operation has the same parameters as replace_string_in_file: filePath, oldString, newString, and explanation. This tool is ideal when you need to make multiple edits across different files or multiple edits in the same file. The tool will provide a summary of successful and failed operations.

explanation.description: A brief explanation of what the multi-replace operation will accomplish.

replacements.description: An array of replacement operations to apply sequentially.

filePath.description: An absolute path to the file to edit.

oldString.description: The exact literal text to replace, preferably unescaped. Include at least 3 lines of context BEFORE and AFTER the target text, matching whitespace and indentation precisely. If this string is not the exact literal text or does not match exactly, this replacement will fail.

newString.description: The exact literal text to replace `oldString` with, preferably unescaped. Provide the EXACT text. Ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic.

tools.name: copilot_readFile
tools.description:
Read the contents of a file.

You must specify the line range you're interested in. Line numbers are 1-indexed. If the file contents returned are insufficient for your task, you may call this tool again to retrieve more content. Prefer reading larger ranges over doing many small reads. Binary files use startLine/endLine as byte offsets.

filePath.description: The absolute path of the file to read.

startLine.description: The line number to start reading from, 1-based.

endLine.description: The inclusive line number to end reading at, 1-based.

tools.name: copilot_readNotebookCellOutput
tools.description: This tool will retrieve the output for a notebook cell from its most recent execution or restored from disk. The cell may have output even when it has not been run in the current kernel session. This tool has a higher token limit for output length than the runNotebookCell tool.

filePath.description: An absolute path to the notebook file with the cell to run, or the URI of a untitled, not yet named, file, such as `untitled:Untitled-1.ipynb

cellId.description: The ID of the cell for which output should be retrieved.

tools.name: copilot_readProjectStructure
tools.description: Get a file tree representation of the workspace.

tools.name: copilot_replaceString
tools.description:
This is a tool for making edits in an existing file in the workspace. For moving or renaming files, use run in terminal tool with the 'mv' command instead. For larger edits, split them into smaller edits and call the edit tool multiple times to ensure accuracy. Before editing, always ensure you have the context to understand the file's contents and context. To edit a file, provide: 1) filePath (absolute path), 2) oldString (MUST be the exact literal text to replace including all whitespace, indentation, newlines, and surrounding code etc), and 3) newString (MUST be the exact literal text to replace \`oldString\` with (also including all whitespace, indentation, newlines, and surrounding code etc.). Ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic.). Each use of this tool replaces exactly ONE occurrence of oldString.

CRITICAL for \`oldString\`: Must uniquely identify the single instance to change. Include at least 3 lines of context BEFORE and AFTER the target text, matching whitespace and indentation precisely. If this string matches multiple locations, or does not match exactly, the tool will fail. Never use 'Lines 123-456 omitted' from summarized documents or ...existing code... comments in the oldString or newString.

filePath.description: An absolute path to the file to edit.

oldString.description: The exact literal text to replace, preferably unescaped. For single replacements (default), include at least 3 lines of context BEFORE and AFTER the target text, matching whitespace and indentation precisely. For multiple replacements, specify expected_replacements parameter. If this string is not the exact literal text (i.e. you escaped it) or does not match exactly, the tool will fail.

newString.description: The exact literal text to replace `old_string` with, preferably unescaped. Provide the EXACT text. Ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic.

tools.name: copilot_resolveMemoryFileUri
tools.description: Resolve a memory file path (like /memories/session/plan.md or /memories/repo/notes.md) to its fully qualified URI. Use this when you need the actual URI for a memory file, for example to pass it to setArtifacts. The path must start with /memories/.

path.description: The memory file path to resolve (e.g. /memories/session/plan.md).

tools.name: copilot_runNotebookCell
tools.description: This is a tool for running a code cell in a notebook file directly in the notebook editor. The output from the execution will be returned. Code cells should be run as they are added or edited when working through a problem to bring the kernel state up to date and ensure the code executes successfully. Code cells are ready to run and don't require any pre-processing. If asked to run the first cell in a notebook, you should run the first code cell since markdown cells cannot be executed. NOTE: Avoid executing Markdown cells or providing Markdown cell IDs, as Markdown cells cannot be  executed.

filePath.description: An absolute path to the notebook file with the cell to run, or the URI of a untitled, not yet named, file, such as `untitled:Untitled-1.ipynb

reason.description: An optional explanation of why the cell is being run. This will be shown to the user before the tool is run and is not necessary if it's self-explanatory.

cellId.description: The ID for the code cell to execute. Avoid providing markdown cell IDs as nothing will be executed.

continueOnError.description: Whether or not execution should continue for remaining cells if an error is encountered. Default to false unless instructed otherwise.

tools.name: copilot_runVscodeCommand
tools.description: Run a command in VS Code. Use this tool to run a command in Visual Studio Code as part of a new workspace creation process only.

commandId.description: The ID of the command to execute. This should be in the format <command>.

name.description: The name of the command to execute. This should be a clear and concise description of the command.

args.description: The arguments to pass to the command. This should be an array of strings.

skipCheck.description: If true, skip checking whether the command exists before executing it.

tools.name: copilot_searchCodebase
tools.description: Run a natural language search for relevant code or documentation comments from the user's current workspace. Returns relevant code snippets from the user's current workspace if it is large, or the full contents of the workspace if it is small.

query.description: The query to search the codebase for. Should contain all relevant context. Should ideally be text that might appear in the codebase, such as function names, variable names, or comments.

tools.name: copilot_searchWorkspaceSymbols
tools.description: Search the user's workspace for code symbols using language services. Use this tool when the user is looking for a specific symbol in their workspace.

symbolName.description: The symbol to search for, such as a function name, class name, or variable name.

tools.name: copilot_sessionStoreSql
tools.description:
Query the local session store containing history from past coding sessions. Uses SQLite SQL syntax.

Actions: 'query' (execute SQL — supports JOINs, FTS5 MATCH, aggregations), 'standup' (pre-fetch last 24h data), 'reindex' (rebuild index from debug logs).

action.description: The action to perform. 'query' (default) executes a SQL query. 'standup' pre-fetches last 24h session data for standup reports. 'reindex' rebuilds the local session index and syncs to cloud if enabled.

query.description: A single read-only SQL query to execute. Required when action is 'query'. Supports SELECT, WITH, JOINs, aggregations, and FTS5 MATCH. Only one statement per call — do not combine multiple queries with semicolons.

force.description: When true with action 'reindex', re-processes all sessions including already-indexed ones. Default false (skips already-indexed sessions).

description.description: A 2-5 word summary of what this call does (e.g. 'Recent sessions overview', 'Generate standup', 'Reindex sessions').

tools.name: copilot_switchAgent
tools.description:
Switch to the Plan agent to align on approach before implementing. Plan will explore the codebase, gathers context, clarifies requirements with the user, and creates an actionable implementation plan.

SWITCH TO PLAN when ANY of these apply:
1. Adding new functionality - where should it go? What patterns to follow?
2. Multiple valid approaches exist - choosing between technologies, patterns, or strategies
3. Modifying existing behavior - unclear what should change or what side effects exist
4. Architectural decisions required - choosing between design patterns or integration approaches
5. Changes span multiple files - refactoring, migrations, or cross-cutting concerns
6. Requirements are underspecified - need to explore before understanding scope

EXAMPLES:
✓ Switch to Plan:
- "Add authentication to the app" → architectural decisions needed (session vs JWT, middleware)
- "Refactor this data flow" → must understand component dependencies first
- "Migrate from X to Y" → requires understanding current structure

✗ Do NOT switch to Plan:
- User attached a detailed spec, plan, or requirements doc → context already provided
- You already started editing files in this conversation → too late to switch
- Single obvious change like fixing a typo or renaming → just do it
- User gave explicit step-by-step instructions → follow them directly

agentName.description: The name of the agent to switch to. Currently only 'Plan' is supported.

tools.name: copilot_viewImage
tools.description: View the contents of an image file. Use this instead of read_file for supported image files such as png, jpg, jpeg, gif, and webp. The tool returns the image directly to multimodal models and does not take line ranges or offsets.

filePath.description: The absolute path of the image file to view.

tools.name: create_and_run_task
tools.description: Creates and runs a build, run, or custom task for the workspace by generating or adding to a tasks.json file based on the project structure (such as package.json or README.md). If the user asks to build, run, launch and they have no tasks.json file, use this tool. If they ask to create or add a task, use this tool.

workspaceFolder.description: The absolute path of the workspace folder where the tasks.json file will be created.

task.description: The task to add to the new tasks.json file.

type.description: The type of the task. The only supported value is 'shell'.

command.description: The shell command to run for the task. Use this to specify commands for building or running the application.

args.description: The arguments to pass to the command.

isBackground.description: Whether the task runs in the background without blocking the UI or other tasks. tools.name: execution_subagent
tools.description:
Launch an iterative execution-focused subagent that performs an execution-based task.
USE THIS INSTEAD OF RUNNING INDIVIDUAL COMMANDS WITH run_in_terminal EXCEPT IN THE RARE CASES THAT YOU NEED THE FULL OUTPUT OF A COMMAND.
Here are some examples of how it can be used:
- Run tests and filter the output to summarize which tests failed and why.
- Install all dependencies of a project.
Returns: A list of commands that were run, along with relevant excerpts of each command's output.
Input fields:
- query: What to execute, and what to look for in the output. Can include exact commands to run, or a description of an execution task.
- description: Short user-visible invocation message.
NOTE: In the subagent query, make sure to specify any restrictions or guidelines on running commands provided by the user earlier in the conversation.
For example, if the user instructs the agent to not edit files in a particular directory, make sure to include that instruction in the subagent query when relevant.

query.description: What to execute, and what to look for in the output. Can include exact commands to run, or a description of an execution task.

tools.name: manage_todo_list
tools.description:
Manage a structured todo list to track progress and plan tasks throughout your coding session. Use this tool VERY frequently to ensure task visibility and proper planning.

When to use this tool:
- Complex multi-step work requiring planning and tracking
- When user provides multiple tasks or requests (numbered/comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions that require multiple steps
- BEFORE starting work on any todo (mark as in-progress)
- IMMEDIATELY after completing each todo (mark completed individually)
- When breaking down larger tasks into smaller actionable steps
- To give users visibility into your progress and planning

When NOT to use:
- Single, trivial tasks that can be completed in one step
- Purely conversational/informational requests
- When just reading files or performing simple searches

CRITICAL workflow:
1. Plan tasks by writing todo list with specific, actionable items
2. Mark ONE todo as in-progress before starting work
3. Complete the work for that specific todo
4. Mark that todo as completed IMMEDIATELY
5. Move to next todo and repeat

Todo states:
- not-started: Todo not yet begun
- in-progress: Currently working (limit ONE at a time)
- completed: Finished successfully

IMPORTANT: Mark todos completed as soon as they are done. Do not batch completions.

todoList.description: Complete array of all todo items. Must include ALL items - both existing and new.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo. Use sequential numbers starting from 1.

title.description: Concise action-oriented todo label (3-7 words). Displayed in UI.

status.description: not-started: Not begun | in-progress: Currently working (max 1) | completed: Fully finished with no blockers

tools.name: notebook
tools.description: Manage lab notebooks in Discovery. WIKI EDITING PROTOCOL: When promoting content from INBOX to the Overview, edit overview.md and INBOX.md DIRECTLY using VS Code file edits — do NOT call promote_to_page or stage_promotion. Append content to overview.md under the appropriate heading, then strikethrough the promoted entry in INBOX.md. The system detects your file edits automatically. NO-SUMMARY RULE: NEVER summarize, paraphrase, or compress content. Preserve ALL formatting, bullet points, data tables, and structure exactly as they appear. The only permitted modifications are: adjusting heading levels, fixing broken markdown syntax, and removing provenance metadata (lines starting with '> Imported' or '> From:'). CONTRIBUTE RULE: When the user asks to contribute/add/save content to a notebook, pass the EXACT FULL TEXT as the 'text' parameter to notebook.triage. Do NOT summarize. CORRECTION RULE: When the user corrects a previous contribution, pass supersedes='{title}' so the old entry is replaced. TRIAGE ACTIONS: Use 'notebook.triage' to add content to INBOX. Use 'notebook.inbox_status' to check pending items. Use 'notebook.list' to see notebooks. Use 'notebook.analyze_triage' for AI-assisted recommendations. Use 'notebook.validate_promotion' after editing files to verify quality. Use 'notebook.optimize_page' for page cleanup. Use 'notebook.dismiss_inbox_item' to remove items. DIRECT EDIT RULES: When triaging, do NOT present raw markdown in your chat response — edit the files directly and report only your recommendation (Item N, Recommendation, Placement, Merge, Rationale). The file edits speak for themselves.

params.description: Action-specific parameters (e.g. notebookId, title, content, cellType, provenance)

tools.name: purpose
tools.description: Manage purpose-driven quality for a project. PIPELINE: (1) set purpose with title+statement, (2) create outcomes (proof points), (3) create or generate rubrics with questions, passingCriteria, and optional evaluationStrategy, (4) grade outcomes using 'grade.run', 'grade.submit', or 'grade.submit-manual', and (5) check 'progress'. Grading auto-cascades outcome status (Achieved/PartiallyAchieved/NotAchieved). Use 'outcome.evaluate' to re-derive status from latest grade.

action.description: The purpose operation to perform. Pipeline: set -> outcome.create -> rubric.generate -> grade.run (with grader) or grade.submit / grade.submit-manual -> progress. Use grader.list to discover available graders (scorecard, regex, llm).

title.description: Title for purpose (set/update), outcome (outcome.create/update), or rubric

outcomeId.description: Outcome ID — required for outcome.get, outcome.update, outcome.delete, outcome.evaluate, grade.run, grade.submit, grade.submit-manual, grade.list, grade.latest, grade.history

rubricId.description: Rubric ID — required for rubric.get, rubric.update, rubric.delete, grade.submit, and grade.submit-manual

gradeId.description: Grade ID (for grade.get — retrieve a specific grade record)

graderId.description: Grader ID for grade.run or grader CRUD. Use grader.list to discover available graders. Built-in: 'scorecard' (pre-scored JSON), 'regex' (pattern matching). Use grader.create to register new graders (script, threshold) that persist across sessions.

artifactRef.description: File path to the artifact to grade (for grade.run). For scorecard grader: JSON file with {rubricId, answers: [{questionId, score, evidence?}]}. For regex grader: text file to scan.

questionScores.description: Pre-scored question results for grade.submit. Array of {questionId, normalizedScore (0-1), rawValue?, reasoning?}. Must cover every question in the rubric.

questions.description: Rubric questions for create or update. Each item can include answerFormat, likertScale, scriptScoring, weight, and evaluationGuidance.

passingCriteria.description: Rubric passing criteria for create or update.

evaluationStrategy.description: Optional grading strategy for rubric create or update.

gradedBy.description: Who produced this grade (for grade.submit). E.g., 'ci-pipeline', 'human:username', 'test-harness'.

type.description: Outcome type for outcome.create: Artifact, Measurement, Decision, Knowledge, or Capability

status.description: Outcome status for outcome.update: Pending, InProgress, Achieved, PartiallyAchieved, or NotAchieved

outcomeIds.description: Array of outcome IDs (for rubric.generate — generates a rubric for each outcome)

taskId.description: Task ID — for outcome.link-task, outcome.unlink-task, or grade.run/grade.submit/grade.submit-manual to associate a grade with a task

reasoning.description: Optional overall grading rationale for submit or submit-manual.

suggestions.description: Optional follow-up suggestions for submit or submit-manual.

count.description: Number of outcomes to suggest (for suggest-outcomes)

command.description: Script command for grader.create with type 'script'. The executable path (e.g. 'pwsh', 'python3', 'node'). Use {{artifact_path}} in args for the artifact file path.

config.description: Type-specific grader configuration for grader.create/update. For script: {command, args}. For threshold: {metric, operator, value, questionId}.

tools.name: renderMermaidDiagram

tools.name: run_in_terminal
tools.description:
This tool allows you to execute Windows PowerShell 5.1 commands in a persistent terminal session, preserving environment variables, working directory, and other context across multiple commands.

Command Execution:
- Use semicolons ; to chain commands on one line, NEVER use && even when asked explicitly
- Prefer pipelines | for object-based data flow
- Never create a sub-shell (eg. powershell -c "command") unless explicitly asked

Directory Management:
- Prefer relative paths when navigating directories, only use absolute when the path is far away or the current cwd is not expected
- By default (mode=sync), shell and cwd are reused by subsequent sync commands
- Use $PWD or Get-Location for current directory
- Use Push-Location/Pop-Location for directory stack

Program Execution:
- Supports .NET, Python, Node.js, and other executables
- Install modules via Install-Module, Install-Package
- Use Get-Command to verify cmdlet/function availability

Async Mode:
- Use mode=async ONLY for processes that should keep running while you do other work (servers, watchers, dev daemons)
- For one-shot long-running commands where you have nothing to do until they finish (package installs, builds, downloads, test suites), use mode=sync with a generous timeout (e.g. 600000 / 10 min for installs, longer for big builds) so the command can complete before your turn ends
- Returns a terminal ID for checking status and runtime later
- Use Start-Job for background PowerShell jobs

Use send_to_terminal to send commands or input to a terminal session.

Output Management:
- Output is automatically truncated if longer than 60KB to prevent context overflow
- Use Select-Object, Where-Object, Format-Table to filter output
- Use -First/-Last parameters to limit results
- For pager commands, add | Out-String or | Format-List

Best Practices:
- Use proper cmdlet names instead of aliases in scripts
- Quote paths with spaces: "C:\Path With Spaces"
- Prefer PowerShell cmdlets over external commands when available
- Prefer idiomatic PowerShell like Get-ChildItem instead of dir or ls for file listings
- Use Test-Path to check file/directory existence
- Be specific with Select-Object properties to avoid excessive output
- Avoid printing credentials unless absolutely required
- NEVER run Start-Sleep or similar wait commands. You will be automatically notified on your next turn when async terminal commands or timed-out sync commands complete or need input. Do NOT poll for completion.

Interactive Input Handling:
- When a terminal command is waiting for interactive input, do NOT suggest alternatives or ask the user whether to proceed. Instead, use the vscode_askQuestions tool to collect the needed values from the user, then send them.
- NEVER use vscode_askQuestions to request sensitive input such as passwords, passphrases, API keys, tokens, or other secrets — answers to that tool are sent through the model. If the prompt requires a secret, tell the user to type it directly into the terminal and stop; do not call vscode_askQuestions or send_to_terminal for that prompt.
- Send exactly one answer per prompt using send_to_terminal. Never send multiple answers in a single send.
- After each send, call get_terminal_output to read the next prompt before sending the next answer.
- Continue one prompt at a time until the command finishes.

Execution mode:
- mode='sync': wait for completion (optionally capped by timeout); if still running when timeout elapses, return with a terminal ID.
- mode='async': wait for an initial idle/output signal, then return with terminal output snapshot and ID. Timeout caps how long to wait for the initial idle/output signal.
- Prefer mode='sync' for commands that will prompt for interactive input (e.g., npm init, interactive installers, configuration wizards).

Timeout parameter: For one-shot long-running commands, set a generous timeout as a safety net (e.g. 600000 for installs, longer for big builds). Omit timeout only for processes that should run indefinitely (servers, daemons). If the timeout elapses, you get a terminal ID and can check output later.

Terminal notifications: When an async command finishes or a sync command times out, you will be automatically notified on your next turn with the exit code and terminal output. You will also be notified if the terminal needs input. Do NOT poll or sleep to wait for completion.

command.description: The command to run in the terminal.

explanation.description: A one-sentence description of what the command does. This will be shown to the user before the command is run.

goal.description: A short description of the goal or purpose of the command (e.g., "Install dependencies", "Start development server").

enumDescriptions: Wait for completion up to timeout, then return with collected output. If still running at timeout, the terminal session continues in the background.
Wait for an initial idle/output signal, then return with a terminal ID and output snapshot while the session may continue running.

isBackground.description: Legacy execution mode flag. Deprecated in favor of "mode". If true, equivalent to mode=async. If false, equivalent to mode=sync.

timeout.description: Optional hard cap in milliseconds on how long the tool tracks the command before returning. Omit to let the command run to completion (recommended for package installs, builds, and long-running scripts). Use 0 to explicitly indicate no timeout.

tools.name: run_task
tools.description:
Runs a VS Code task.

- If you see that an appropriate task exists for building or running code, prefer to use this tool to run the task instead of using the run_in_terminal tool.
- Make sure that any appropriate build or watch task is running before trying to run tests or execute code.
- If the user asks to run a task, use this tool to do so.

workspaceFolder.description: The workspace folder path containing the task

tools.name: runSubagent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. This tool is good at researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries, use this agent to perform the search for you.

- Agents do not run async or in the background, you will wait for the agent's result.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the user asks for a certain agent, you MUST provide that EXACT agent name (case-sensitive) to invoke that specific agent.

prompt.description: A detailed description of the task for the agent to perform

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

agentName.description: Optional name of a specific agent to invoke. If not provided, uses the current agent.

model.description: Optional model for the subagent. Format: "Model Name (Vendor)", vendor is usually "copilot". Only use to enforce a specific model.

tools.name: runTests
tools.description: Runs unit tests in files. Use this tool if the user asks to run tests or when you want to validate changes using unit tests, and prefer using this tool instead of the terminal tool. When possible, always try to provide `files` paths containing the relevant unit tests in order to avoid unnecessarily long test runs. This tool outputs detailed information about the results of the test run. Set mode="coverage" to also collect coverage and optionally provide coverageFiles for focused reporting.

files.description: Absolute paths to the test files to run. If not provided, all test files will be run.

testNames.description: An array of test names to run. Depending on the context, test names defined in code may be strings or the names of functions or classes containing the test cases. If not provided, all tests in the files will be run.

mode.description: Execution mode: "run" (default) runs tests normally, "coverage" collects coverage.

coverageFiles.description: When mode="coverage": absolute file paths to include detailed coverage info for. If not provided, a file-level summary of all files with incomplete coverage is shown.

Launch a fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?").
Returns: A list of relevant files/snippet locations in the workspace.

Input fields:
- query: Natural language description of what to search for.
- description: Short user-visible invocation message. 
- details: 2-3 sentences detailing the objective of the search agent.

tools.name: send_to_terminal
tools.description: Send input text to an active terminal execution (identified by the `id` returned from run_in_terminal). The 'command' field may be empty or whitespace to press Enter (useful for interactive prompts). By default, returns the last 20 lines of terminal output captured shortly after sending. Set 'waitForOutput' to true for interactive programs (games, REPLs, etc.) to wait until the terminal becomes idle before returning output — this gives you the program's response to your input.

id.description: The ID of an active terminal execution to send a command to (returned by run_in_terminal for async executions, or for sync executions that timed out and were moved to the background).

command.description: The input text to send to the terminal. The text is sent followed by Enter. Provide an empty or whitespace string to send just Enter (for interactive prompts).

waitForOutput.description: When true, waits for the terminal to become idle (no new output for a short period) before returning, instead of returning immediately. Use this for interactive programs where you need to see the full response to your input. Defaults to false.

tools.name: skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill to handle a user's request with specialized instructions and workflows.

Skills are domain-specific capabilities discovered from SKILL.md files. When a user's task matches an available skill, call this tool to load and apply it. If the user types a slash command (e.g. "/deploy", "/test"), treat it as a skill invocation.

Usage:
- Pass the skill name only (no arguments).
- Examples: skill: "docx", skill: "deploy", skill: "fix-ci-failures"

Rules:
- Available skills appear in system-reminder messages earlier in the conversation.
- BLOCKING: When a matching skill exists, you MUST call this tool before producing any other output about the task.
- Never reference a skill without calling this tool.
- Do not call this tool for a skill that is already active in the current turn (indicated by a <command-name> tag).
- Do not use this tool for built-in commands such as /help or /clear.

tools.name: task_complete
tools.description:
Signal that the user's task is fully done. You MUST call this tool when your work is complete — whether you made code changes, answered a question, or completed any other kind of task. Provide a brief summary of what was accomplished. Do not restate the summary in your message text — it is shown to the user directly.

IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, you MUST output a brief text message summarizing what was done. The task is not complete until both your summary message AND this tool call are present.

When to call:
- After answering the user's question or completing a conversational request
- After you have completed ALL requested changes
- After verifying results: tests pass, terminal commands succeeded, tool calls returned expected output

When NOT to call:
- If a terminal command failed or produced unexpected output
- If an MCP or external tool call returned an error
- If you encountered errors you have not resolved
- If there are remaining steps to complete
- If you have not verified your changes work

summary.description: Brief summary of what was accomplished. Omit for trivial interactions.

tools.name: tasks
tools.description: Manage Discovery tasks, dependency graphs, and flow templates. Task statuses (camelCase): new, executing, executionDone, complete, onHold, failed, incomplete, stale, flaggedHuman, flaggedAi, removed. Status input is case-insensitive. Transitions follow a strict state machine — invalid transitions return INVALID_TRANSITION with allowedStatuses. Use 'transition' to change status (parameter name is 'status', NOT 'to'). Common wrong values: 'done', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'pending', 'closed' are ALL invalid — use the exact enum values above. NEVER modify task JSON files on disk directly; always use this tool. Use 'ready' (query) to find tasks whose dependencies are all complete or executionDone. Use 'blocked' (query) to find tasks with unmet dependencies. Delete is non-cascading by default; fails with HAS_CHILDREN if the task has children unless cascade=true (recursive is accepted as an alias). findByTitle uses fuzzy scoring, not exact match. Flows are workspace-configurable templates; listFlows returns [] if none are configured.

action.description: The task or flow action to perform. Mutations: create, update, transition, assign, delete, comment, decompose, addSubtask, move, addDependency, removeDependency, instantiateFlow. Queries: get, getMany, list, ready, blocked, graph, findByTitle, subtreeSummary, dependencyGraph, listFlows, flowStatus, listFlowInstances.

taskId.description: Task ID or DX reference (e.g. DX-42 or #42). Required for: get, update, transition, assign, delete, comment, decompose, addSubtask, move, addDependency, removeDependency, subtreeSummary, dependencyGraph. Optional for graph (used as rootId).

taskIds.description: Task IDs or DX references for batch retrieval actions

title.description: Task title for create or decompose actions

description.description: Optional task description for create or update

parentId.description: Parent task ID. For create: creates a subtask under this parent. For addSubtask: required parent. For move: new parent to move task under. For instantiateFlow: optional parent for the flow root task.

rootId.description: Root task ID for graph action. If omitted, returns the full workspace graph.

dependsOnId.description: Target dependency task ID for addDependency and removeDependency actions. The task identified by taskId will depend on this task.

targetIndex.description: Target sibling position index for the move action (0-based).

recursive.description: For delete action: alias for cascade. If true, deletes the task and all its descendants. If false (default), delete fails with HAS_CHILDREN when children exist.

cascade.description: For delete action: if true, deletes the task and all its descendants. If false (default), delete fails with HAS_CHILDREN when children exist. Preferred over 'recursive'.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return for findByTitle (default: 10).

view.description: Optional projected response shape for get/list/search actions

fields.description: Optional explicit task field projection for get/list/search actions

status.description: Target task status for the transition action. Must be one of the enum values: new, executing, executionDone, complete, onHold, failed, incomplete, stale, flaggedHuman, flaggedAi, removed. Common wrong values that will be rejected: 'done', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'pending', 'closed'. Use the parameter name 'status' (not 'to' or 'state'). Also usable as a filter value for list actions.

text.description: Comment text for comment action. Required for comment.

comment.description: Optional comment to record with a transition action.

createdBy.description: Optional actor identifier to record with a comment. Use this when posting on behalf of an agent, engine, application, or system.

createdByType.description: Optional actor type to record with a comment. Use User, Application, Engine, System, or Agent. Defaults to User when omitted.

triggeredBy.description: Optional identifier for who or what triggered a transition.

assignedTo.description: Assignee for create or assign actions. Omit to unassign. For assign, omitting assignedTo clears the current assignee.

id.description: Assignee identifier (e.g. 'copilot', a username, or an engine instance ID). Not validated against a directory.

type.description: Type of assignee. Defaults to User if omitted.

labels.description: Task labels for create or update

acceptanceCriteria.description: Acceptance criteria for create or update

sourceType.description: Content kind, for example file, notebookEntry, or storageAsset. Defaults to file.

uri.description: URI or path for the created content.

title.description: Optional display title for the created content.

createdContent.description: Content created while completing the task, such as workspace files

subtasks.description: Subtask titles (strings) or objects with title and optional description, for the decompose action. Creates child tasks under the specified taskId.

flowId.description: Flow definition ID for instantiateFlow. Obtain IDs from listFlows.

instanceId.description: Flow instance ID for flowStatus. Obtain IDs from instantiateFlow or listFlowInstances.

parameters.description: Optional parameters for instantiateFlow, passed to the flow template.

tools.name: terminal_last_command
tools.description: Get the last command run in the active terminal.

tools.name: terminal_selection
tools.description: Get the current selection in the active terminal.

tools.name: testFailure
tools.description: Includes test failure information in the prompt. Use this tool to get the details of test failures from the most recent test run. If there are no failures yet, suggest running tests first.

tools.name: tools
tools.description: Search, install, and call tools from the Discovery catalog. Actions: (1) 'search' — find plugins by keyword, returns pluginName, callable status, and tool names. (2) 'list' — show all installed plugins with tools. (3) 'call' — invoke a tool using pluginName + toolName + arguments. (4) 'install' — install a metadata_only plugin from a marketplace to make it callable. (5) 'uninstall' — remove an installed plugin. WORKFLOW: search → if callable=true, call directly; if status='metadata_only', install first, then call. ALWAYS search or list first — never guess pluginName or toolName. Example: action='search', query='cloudflare' → finds pluginName='cloudflare' with callable=true → action='call', pluginName='cloudflare', toolName='search', arguments={query:'zones'}. For metadata_only: action='install', pluginName='my-plugin' → installs and returns available tools → action='call'.

action.description: The operation: 'search' to find plugins, 'list' to see all plugins, 'call' to invoke a tool, 'install' to install a metadata_only plugin, 'uninstall' to remove a plugin

query.description: Natural language search query (for 'search' action) — e.g. 'life science research' or 'email meetings'

tools.name: vscode_askQuestions
tools.description: Use this tool to ask the user a small number of clarifying questions before proceeding. Provide the questions array with concise headers and prompts. Use options for fixed choices, set multiSelect when multiple selections are allowed. Users can always provide a freeform text answer alongside options unless you set allowFreeformInput to false.

questions.description: List of questions to ask the user. Order is preserved.

header.description: Short identifier for the question. Must be unique so answers can be mapped back to the question. Maximum 50 characters.

question.description: The question text to display to the user. Keep it concise, ideally one sentence. Maximum 200 characters.

multiSelect.description: Allow selecting multiple options when options are provided.

allowFreeformInput.description: Allow freeform text answers in addition to option selection. Defaults to true; set to false to restrict to predefined options only.

message.description: Optional markdown message to display below the question text, providing additional context or details.

options.description: Optional list of selectable answers. If omitted, the question is free text.

label.description: Display label and value for the option.

description.description: Optional secondary text shown with the option.

recommended.description: Mark this option as the recommended default.

tools.name: vscode_get_terminal_confirmation
tools.description:
This tool allows you to get explicit user confirmation for a terminal command without executing it.

When to use:
- When you need to verify user approval before executing a command
- When you want to show command details, auto-approval status, and simplified versions to the user
- When you need the user to review a potentially risky command

The tool will:
- Show the command with syntax highlighting
- Display auto-approval status if enabled
- Show simplified version of the command if applicable
- Provide custom actions for creating auto-approval rules
- Return approval/rejection status

After confirmation, use a tool to actually execute the command.

command.description: The command to confirm with the user.

explanation.description: A one-sentence description of what the command does. This will be shown to the user in the confirmation dialog.

goal.description: A short description of the goal or purpose of the command.

mode.description: Execution mode this command would use if run.

tools.name: vscode_listCodeUsages
tools.description:
Find all usages (references, definitions, and implementations) of a code symbol across the workspace. This tool locates where a symbol is referenced, defined, or implemented.

Input:
- "symbol": The exact name of the symbol to search for (function, class, method, variable, type, etc.).
- "uri": A full URI (e.g. "file:///path/to/file.ts") of a file where the symbol appears. Provide either "uri" or "filePath".
- "filePath": A workspace-relative file path (e.g. "src/utils/helpers.ts") of a file where the symbol appears. Provide either "uri" or "filePath".
- "lineContent": A substring of the line of code where the symbol appears. This is used to locate the exact position in the file. Must be the actual text from the file - do NOT fabricate it.

IMPORTANT: The file and line do NOT need to be the definition of the symbol. Any occurrence works - a usage, an import, a call site, etc. You can pick whichever occurrence is most convenient.

If the tool returns an error, retry with corrected input - ensure the file path is correct, the line content matches the actual file content, and the symbol name appears in that line.

If the file's language has no reference provider registered, the tool returns an error.

symbol.description: The exact name of the symbol (function, class, method, variable, type, etc.) to find usages of.

uri.description: A full URI of a file where the symbol appears (e.g. "file:///path/to/file.ts"). Provide either "uri" or "filePath".

filePath.description: A workspace-relative file path where the symbol appears (e.g. "src/utils/helpers.ts"). Provide either "uri" or "filePath".

lineContent.description: A substring of the line of code where the symbol appears. Used to locate the exact position. Must be actual text from the file.

tools.name: vscode_renameSymbol
tools.description:
Rename a code symbol across the workspace using the language server's rename functionality. This performs a precise, semantics-aware rename that updates all references.

Input:
- "symbol": The exact current name of the symbol to rename.
- "newName": The new name for the symbol.
- "uri": A full URI (e.g. "file:///path/to/file.ts") of a file where the symbol appears. Provide either "uri" or "filePath".
- "filePath": A workspace-relative file path (e.g. "src/utils/helpers.ts") of a file where the symbol appears. Provide either "uri" or "filePath".
- "lineContent": A substring of the line of code where the symbol appears. This is used to locate the exact position in the file. Must be the actual text from the file - do NOT fabricate it.

IMPORTANT: The file and line do NOT need to be the definition of the symbol. Any occurrence works - a usage, an import, a call site, etc. You can pick whichever occurrence is most convenient.

If the tool returns an error, retry with corrected input - ensure the file path is correct, the line content matches the actual file content, and the symbol name appears in that line.

If the file's language has no rename provider registered, the tool returns an error.

symbol.description: The exact current name of the symbol to rename.

newName.description: The new name for the symbol.

uri.description: A full URI of a file where the symbol appears (e.g. "file:///path/to/file.ts"). Provide either "uri" or "filePath".

filePath.description: A workspace-relative file path where the symbol appears (e.g. "src/utils/helpers.ts"). Provide either "uri" or "filePath".

tools.name: vscode_reviewPlan
tools.description: Use this tool to present a plan to the user for review. Provide the plan content as markdown, a list of approval actions (with optional default), and whether the user can provide freeform feedback. Optionally provide a URI to the backing plan file so the user can edit it. The tool returns the chosen action, whether the plan was rejected, and any feedback.

title.description: Title displayed in the widget header. Defaults to "Review plan" if omitted.

plan.description: Optional URI of an editable plan file. An Edit button in the widget header opens it in the editor.

content.description: Markdown content rendered in the body of the widget. May be the plan summary or full plan text.

actions.description: List of approval actions offered in the primary dropdown button. Order is preserved.

label.description: Short action label shown in the dropdown button.

description.description: Optional detail shown below the label in the dropdown list.

default.description: Whether this action should be selected by default.

permissionLevel.description: When set to "autopilot", a confirmation dialog is shown before proceeding.

canProvideFeedback.description: When true, an additional feedback textarea is shown below the plan content.

tools.name: vscode_searchExtensions_internal
tools.description: This is a tool for browsing Visual Studio Code Extensions Marketplace. It allows the model to search for extensions and retrieve detailed information about them. The model should use this tool whenever it needs to discover extensions or resolve information about known ones. To use the tool, the model has to provide the category of the extensions, relevant search keywords, or known extension IDs. Note that search results may include false positives, so reviewing and filtering is recommended.

category.description: The category of extensions to search for

ids.description: The ids of the extensions to search for
